definition: tool_sequence — the calls the caller expected against the calls the agent made, compared in a mode. strict: the actual calls equal the expected, pairwise and in order, with nothing beyond them. unordered: equal as multisets — every expected call consumed by a distinct actual call, none left over. subset: every expected call has SOME matching actual call (set semantics; extras and repeats allowed). superset: every actual call matches SOME expected call (set semantics; omissions and repeats allowed). ordered_subset (the default, and what an unknown mode string falls back to): the expected calls appear in order among the actual ones — each expected call is satisfied by the first later actual call that matches it. A call matches by tool name, and by arguments only when the expectation carries an input: under args exact the normalised inputs must be equal (object keys sorted, whitespace collapsed); under args subset (the default) every key of the expected input must be present in the actual input with the same value, recursively, arrays and scalars compared whole. In a one-to-one matching, an expectation that names arguments is placed before one that does not. The rule FAILS when the mode is not satisfied and SKIPS without a trajectory or without expected calls. Positive = the mode is not satisfied (the rule should FAIL).
source: LLM-authored on 2026-09-21 for arc 9 (N-13). One task narrative (read, grep, write) carried through every mode, then research and test-and-commit narratives; the cases that carry the weight are the boundary pairs per mode (in order vs swapped, present vs missing, an extra call, a repeat), the argument pairs (subset vs exact, a named path that matches vs one that does not, keys in another order, a string against an object) and the unknown-mode pair.
labelling: LLM-authored and LLM-labelled against the documented definition above on 2026-09-21, by reading the expected calls, the actual calls and the mode and applying the definition by hand — a policy family measures conformance to its own definition, so a disagreement here is a rule defect or a definition error, never an opinion about the agent.
